## Story

As a release engineer, when I run the Closure Checks bulk migration on `brainstorm:complete`-tagged epics, a haiku classifier evaluates each SC/DoD/AC item and labels it `end-state`, `transitional`, or `uncertain` with a 1–5 ranking and a rationale — so transitional items are routed to `## Closure Checks` automatically (with explicit per-item user acknowledge) and end-state items stay in `## Success Criteria`, eliminating the manual SC/CC split currently required after the structural migration ships an empty section.

This story re-implements epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 SC6 at the full scope specified in the epic. The existing `migrate-closure-checks.sh` (a structural migration script that adds an empty `## Closure Checks` section) is the **Phase 1** implementation — this story is **Phase 2** that adds the LLM-assisted intelligent classification layer on top.

## Done Definitions (verbatim from epic SC6)

- DD1 (classifier dispatch): `migrate-closure-checks.sh` (Phase 1) is extended with a classifier dispatch step that runs on every `brainstorm:complete`-tagged epic. For each item in the epic's `## Success Criteria`, `## Done Definitions`, and `## Acceptance Criteria` sections, a haiku-tier Anthropic API dispatch is made with a stable JSON-output prompt.

- DD2 (classifier output schema): Each classification returns `{label: "end-state" | "transitional" | "uncertain", ranking: 1-5, rationale: string}`. Schema is validated; malformed responses retry once then escalate.

- DD3 (escalation criteria): Items with `label == "uncertain"` OR `ranking <= 3` are escalated to the user via `AskUserQuestion` (or equivalent CLI prompt). User decision is recorded alongside the classifier output.

- DD4 (per-item explicit acknowledge): No batch-approve. Each item that the classifier proposes to move from SC → CC (or to leave in SC despite being classified `transitional`) requires explicit user acknowledge. Batch acknowledge is prohibited even when items are similar — the UX must force per-item review.

- DD5 (25-item batch cap): Migration review batches are capped at 25 items per batch. After 25 acknowledgments, the script pauses and emits a `BATCH_PAUSE` line; the next batch begins on explicit user resume.

- DD6 (snapshot + idempotent): Migration is snapshot-based. The script captures a stable snapshot of each ticket at the start of a session and operates against that snapshot. Re-runs after the session pick up any tickets edited during prior passes (idempotent for un-edited tickets; re-classified for edited ones).

- DD7 (audit comment per ticket): For each ticket migrated, an audit comment is appended to the ticket recording `{snapshot_timestamp: ISO-8601, original_text: <pre-migration item text>, classification: {label, ranking, rationale}, user_decision: <if escalated>, post_migration_section: "SC" | "CC"}`. Comment schema documented in a contract doc at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/contracts/closure-checks-classifier-audit.md`.

- DD8 (operational dry-run): Script supports `--dry-run` mode that runs the classifier and emits the proposed plan without writing EDIT events or audit comments.

- DD9 (operational migration run): After the tool is built (DD1–DD8) and the Phase 3.5 coherence walkthrough has been run against epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 and reports `overall_verdict: PASS` (per story 5362's tools, executed as epic-level work and recorded as a comment on a03c), the migration is run end-to-end: `migrate-closure-checks.sh --classify --target <host-project-root>` executes against all `brainstorm:complete`-tagged epics. The operator processes per-item acks through the interactive flow, honors batch caps, and resolves uncertain/low-ranking escalations. The `migration_run_id` of this operational run is recorded as a comment on epic a03c-d55e-1393-4f27 with the run's start and end timestamps, total items processed, count migrated SC→CC, and count escalated/deferred.

← Validates Closure Check: "all brainstorm:complete-tagged epics migrated through the classifier carry an audit comment per ticket with snapshot_timestamp, classification, and rationale fields"
← Satisfies: "SC6: plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh dispatches a haiku classifier per SC/DoD/AC item on every brainstorm:complete-tagged epic. Classifier returns {label: end-state|transitional|uncertain, ranking: 1-5, rationale: string}. Escalate to user on label=uncertain OR ranking <= 3. Migration review batches capped at 25 items per batch; per-item explicit acknowledge required (no batch-approve button). Migration is snapshot-based and idempotent — re-runs pick up tickets edited during prior passes. Audit comment per ticket records {snapshot_timestamp, original_text, classification, ranking, rationale}."

## Brainstorm Decisions (locked 2026-05-20)

These five decisions resolve the design ambiguity flagged by the `scrutiny:pending` tag. All decisions stay within the scope of SC6 — no scope expansion beyond what the epic requires.

### §1. Phase 1 integration: augment in place with --classify flag

The Phase 2 classifier layer is added to the existing `migrate-closure-checks.sh` (NOT a new wrapper script). The script gains a `--classify` flag. Without the flag, the script behaves exactly as it does today (structural-only migration that adds an empty `## Closure Checks` section). With the flag, after the structural pass completes, the classifier loop runs over each ticket's items. Both passes share the existing batching, progress-file resume, and idempotency infrastructure.

Rationale: single source of truth, smaller diff, the existing 25-item batch cap and progress-file machinery are reusable as-is.

### §2. Per-item ack UX: script-native interactive prompts on stdin

When `--classify` runs in a TTY, the script shows each proposed migration (label, ranking, rationale, original text, proposed destination) and prompts `[a]ccept / [r]eject / [d]efer` via `read -r`. When stdin is NOT a TTY (piped), the script does not prompt — items needing escalation (per DD3) are added to the audit comment with `user_decision: deferred`, and the script exits non-zero so the caller knows to re-invoke interactively.

Rationale: matches Phase 1's existing TTY/pipe convention, no skill-wrapper surface, the script runs standalone in any terminal.

### §3. Classifier dispatch: inline Anthropic SDK call

The classifier is dispatched inline via the Anthropic Python SDK (same pattern as `closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` built for story 5362). The script requires `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at runtime; without it, the classifier pass is skipped with a `NOTICE` log line and the structural migration still completes (graceful degradation).

Rationale: self-contained script, no orchestrator-side dispatch wrapper needed, consistent with the existing `closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` precedent.

### §4. Audit comment shape: one comment per ticket, JSON body

Each migrated ticket receives ONE audit comment with a JSON body conforming to the contract at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/contracts/closure-checks-classifier-audit.md`:

```json
{
  "snapshot_timestamp": "<ISO-8601>",
  "migration_run_id": "<uuid>",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "items": [
    {
      "original_text": "<verbatim pre-migration item text>",
      "original_section": "SC" | "DD" | "AC",
      "classification": {"label": "end-state" | "transitional" | "uncertain", "ranking": 1-5, "rationale": "<string>"},
      "user_decision": "accept" | "reject" | "defer" | "auto",
      "post_migration_section": "SC" | "CC"
    }
  ]
}
```

`user_decision: "auto"` is used when the classifier returned `end-state` AND `ranking >= 4` (no user prompt — item stayed in SC automatically). The four other values come from the interactive ack UX in §2.

Rationale: machine-parseable, single audit record per ticket, greppable for `migration_run_id`. DD7's "an audit comment" (singular) phrasing matches.

### §5. Snapshot semantics: disk snapshot augmenting Phase 1's progress file

When `--classify` starts a session, the script captures a snapshot of each ticket's `description` field (at audit-time) to `/tmp/migrate-closure-checks-classify.<session-id>.snapshot/<ticket-id>.txt`. Throughout the session, all classification decisions operate against the snapshot, not against live ticket reads (which could change mid-session if another process edits the ticket).

The snapshot directory sits next to Phase 1's existing `/tmp/migrate-closure-checks.<session-id>.progress` file. On resume (re-run with the same session-id), the script checks each ticket's CURRENT description against the snapshot — if they match, skip (already-processed). If they differ, re-snapshot and re-classify that ticket only (DD6 idempotent behavior).

Rationale: durable (survives interruptions), gives DD6 idempotency a concrete mechanism, sits cleanly alongside Phase 1's existing per-session state.

## Approach Summary

Modify `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh`:

1. Add `--classify` flag to the argument parser
2. After the existing structural pass completes (per-ticket `_migrate_ticket` invocation), if `--classify` was passed, run a new `_classify_ticket_items` python function on each migrated ticket
3. The classifier function:
   - Extracts items from `## Success Criteria`, `## Done Definitions`, `## Acceptance Criteria` sections (reuse the regex from `closure-checks-migration-preview.sh`'s `extract_items` helper — DRY)
   - For each item, dispatches haiku via Anthropic SDK; expects JSON output per DD2
   - Validates schema; retries once on malformed; logs ERROR and skips item on second failure
   - On `label == uncertain` OR `ranking <= 3`: enters interactive ack flow via `read -r` (TTY) or appends `user_decision: deferred` (piped)
   - On `label == end-state` AND `ranking >= 4`: auto-accept, no prompt
   - On `label == transitional` AND `ranking >= 4`: enters interactive ack flow (DD4 requires explicit per-item ack for ALL section-changing moves, even high-confidence ones)
4. After all items in a ticket are classified, write the per-ticket audit comment (JSON per §4)
5. Apply the section moves (transitional items move SC→CC; uncertain accepted items follow user decision; rejected items stay in original section)
6. Capture the disk snapshot at session start, check against on resume (§5)
7. Honor the 25-item batch cap across the entire session (across multiple tickets); after 25 acknowledgments, print `BATCH_PAUSE: <N> acknowledgments processed. Re-run to continue.` and exit 0
8. `--dry-run` short-circuits the apply step — emit the proposed plan to stdout, do not write audit comments or EDIT events

Create `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/closure-checks-classifier-audit.md` with `contract_version=1` documenting the JSON schema in §4 and the `migration_run_id` semantics.

Operational run (DD9): after the tool is built and the Phase 3.5 walkthrough has reported PASS against a03c, invoke `migrate-closure-checks.sh --classify` end-to-end. The operator (or this session) processes per-item acks across all brainstorm:complete-tagged epics. On completion, post a comment on epic a03c with the `migration_run_id`, start/end timestamps, item counts, and the post-migration audit-comment locations.

## Relevant Files

Files this story MODIFIES (single modification surface):
- `plugins/dso/scripts/migrate-closure-checks.sh` — add `--classify` flag and classifier loop

Files this story CREATES:
- `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/closure-checks-classifier-audit.md` — `contract_version=1` audit comment JSON schema

Files this story READS (no modification):
- `plugins/dso/scripts/closure-checks-migration-preview.sh` — reuse `extract_items` regex helper for SC/DD/AC item enumeration
- `plugins/dso/scripts/ticket-migrate-closure-checks-v1.sh` — Phase 1 per-ticket logic (already invoked by Phase 1 outer script; unchanged)
- `plugins/dso/skills/shared/prompts/verifiable-sc-check.md` — source for the classifier prompt's accept/reject examples (already on disk from epic a03c earlier work)

## Considerations (post-brainstorm — resolved status)

- **Brainstorming required before implementation-plan**: ✅ RESOLVED — all five open design questions answered above. Ready for implementation.
- **Scope: tools vs. operational completion** (added 2026-05-20): DD9 added per user direction. Closing this story requires the migration to actually execute (not just the tool to be invocable). Tool-builder DDs (DD1–DD8) and operational DD (DD9) co-exist in one story per the (c) path chosen at brainstorm time. Phase 3.5 coherence walkthrough (story 5362's tools) is a prerequisite of DD9 and is tracked as epic-level work on a03c, not as a separate story.
- **Classifier prompt design**: ✅ RESOLVED — reuse the prompt shape already shipped in `closure-checks-migration-preview.sh`, augment with the verifiable-sc-check.md accept/reject examples for richer context.
- **Per-item acknowledge UX**: ✅ RESOLVED — terminal `read -r` (§2).
- **Audit-comment write-path**: ✅ RESOLVED — one comment per ticket with JSON body (§4).
- **Phase 1 dependency**: ✅ already satisfied — Phase 1 is complete and merged.
- **API key dependency**: ✅ RESOLVED — soft-skip with NOTICE log when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` absent (§3); structural migration still completes.
- **Cost model**: 25-item batch cap doubles as fatigue mitigation and cost ceiling. Per-batch cost estimate: at ~12 items per epic and 80 brainstorm:complete-tagged epics, ~960 haiku dispatches total. Document the estimate in the script's `--help` output.

## Escalation Policy

Escalate when blocked — agents proceed unless a significant assumption is required that could send implementation in the wrong direction. All assumptions made without escalating are documented.
